questions.q: What naming habit does this lesson suggest for test records, using the example "Test Account 2026-10"?
options: Dating test data so it still means something months later, unlike a generic name like "Test Account 3"
Never naming test records at all
Using only numbers with no letters in any record name
Naming every record identically to avoid confusion
questions.explain: The lesson recommends dating test data (like "Test Account 2026-10") because it remains meaningful later, unlike a generic numbered name.

questions.q: What does this lesson suggest prefixing custom objects or test records with?
options: The course they belong to, such as "SF-Admin-" or "T-SQL-"
A random number generated by Salesforce
The current user's password
The org's Organization ID
questions.explain: Prefixing by course (like "SF-Admin-") makes it clear later which course a given record or object came from.

questions.q: What is Notes, as described in this lesson?
options: A real, built-in Salesforce object for attaching context to a record, reachable from the App Launcher
A third-party app that must be purchased separately
A feature only available in Developer Edition, not Trailhead Playgrounds
A renamed version of the Reports tab
questions.explain: Notes is a genuine built-in Salesforce object, accessible from the App Launcher's All Items list or directly from record pages.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say naming discipline matters for the Data Import Wizard specifically?
options: Because its field-mapping step only goes smoothly when the source file's column names are clear and consistent
Because the Data Import Wizard renames all incoming records automatically
Because imported records cannot be renamed after import
Because the Data Import Wizard has no connection to naming at all
questions.explain: Clear, consistent column names in the source file make the Data Import Wizard's field-mapping step go smoothly.

questions.q: Does this lesson say a permanent org should accumulate records indefinitely without cleanup?
options: No — it recommends periodically deleting records you're genuinely done with to keep the org navigable
Yes, nothing should ever be deleted from a permanent org
Yes, because deleting records breaks the org
The lesson does not address cleanup at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly recommends periodic cleanup, deleting records you're done with, to keep a permanent org navigable over time.
